_comment: TEMPLATE. setup.sh turns this into ops/jobs.json, which is local to this
robot and is not tracked by git. Edit that copy (here or from the panel's
- the --camera name:serial pairs of the cameras job. Serials are printed
- --arm right | left | both in the teleop job.
ROBOT_ID is not set here: it comes from .env.
stop.signal is SIGINT on purpose. Ctrl+C is the only tested way to stop
the teleop job: it parks the arms. The teleop job is never force-killed
automatically, because a kill in the middle of that leaves an arm latched
in an emergency stop until it is power-cycled.

actions.name: Reclaim CAN control (left)
actions.blurb: Clears a latched emergency stop or teach mode on the left arm so teleop can take command again.
actions.confirm: Sends control-mode messages only: it does not enable motors and cannot move the arm. Afterwards the arm follows commands again, so keep clear of it.

actions.name: Reclaim CAN control (right)
actions.blurb: Clears a latched emergency stop or teach mode on the right arm so teleop can take command again.
actions.confirm: Sends control-mode messages only: it does not enable motors and cannot move the arm. Afterwards the arm follows commands again, so keep clear of it.

stop.force_warning: Force-stopping the cameras only cuts the live video. No hardware risk.

DANGER: force-killing interrupts the arms' controlled stop and can leave an arm latched in an emergency stop with its drivers off. It will not re-enable until you unplug and re-plug its power. Only force when the job is provably stuck.
